fieldValues.title: WG Third-party ready leans Initiator on its domain's three axes
fieldValues.decision_question: Which pole does WG Third-party ready lean toward on each of the three axes of its domain, Semantic records?
fieldValues.context:
Problem: the group role 834b61fd records no lean (control room growth gate 'trigram', 0 of 3), so its compass says nothing about where it pulls when values conflict, and the group cannot pass its Seed gate.
The domain's axes are now one compass axis per T3 line: Attribution and Repository (Space: Office or Testimony), Containment and Portability (Energy: Portability or Possession), Identity and Assertion (Time: Evolution or Continuity). The six Pattern Grid axes (srs docs/charter/decision-compass.md) fall in pairs on the three T3 lines; Identity and Assertion replaced the set-aside Description and Governance in the third slot, because the outline had no Time axis.
The group's purpose now (owner, 2026-10-20): get the spec and the reference implementation ready for public use at speed, before much is built on the spec. It works toward transformation and outward action with a clear deliverable: Initiator mode (Act, Disrupt, Focus).
Why it matters: on the three chosen axes the group and its domain agree (Office, Portability, Evolution). On the paired axes the domain also holds stabilising defaults, Reliability over Renewal (5-11) and Semantic integrity over practical expression (1-7), so an Initiator group pulls against half of each line. When the precommitted Continuity flip of axis 2-8 fires at the first full public release, it pulls against the chosen axis too.
Options and consequences: (a) lean Initiator: Office, Portability, Evolution, bound by the paired defaults as rules; (b) lean with the domain's stabilising pairs (Continuity on Time), which slows the group before any third party depends on the spec; (c) do nothing: the trigram gate stays open and drift cannot be read.
Recommendation: (a).
Action needed: ratify in a session; on ratification assert com.semanticops.method/leans-toward (or the installed leans-toward) from role 834b61fd to poles 221f2e16 (Office), f487d107 (Portability) and 80a1bd7d (Evolution).
Urgency: medium. It is one of two gates keeping the only delegated group from a traceable Seed.
fieldValues.friction: The control room reads WG Third-party ready as operating ahead of its gates: merging and reporting with no recorded compass lean.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
(a) Initiator (Office, Portability, Evolution), with the paired stabilising defaults binding as rules. Leads to fast change now, with drift against the domain visible and bounded.
(b) Steward-like (Office, Possession or Portability, Continuity). Leads to a slower group that matches the domain's eventual phase, before third parties need it.
(c) Do nothing. Leads to an open Seed gate and no reading of drift.
fieldValues.key_requirements: The group keeps the domain's paired defaults as rules: standing contracts hold, and renewal happens only as explicit supersession at a declared boundary (5-11); semantic integrity over practical expression (1-7). Leaning Evolution never licenses a silent break.
fieldValues.decision_statement: WG Third-party ready leans toward Office (Attribution and Repository), Portability (Containment and Portability) and Evolution (Identity and Assertion): the Initiator stance. The domain's paired defaults on axes 5-11 and 1-7 bind it as rules.
fieldValues.rationale: The group exists to change the spec and its implementation quickly while change is still cheap. Its lean should say so, and the drift it makes against its domain should be read rather than hidden.
fieldValues.revisit_when: The Continuity flip of axis 2-8 fires (the first full public release), or the first third party reports a break caused by a change the group made.
